name: Question 10
worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+X+3 \\  & ={X}^{2}+X+3I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(B)={B}^{2}+B+3I.$

Let's calculate ${B}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{2} & =B\cdot B \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(B):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(B) & ={B}^{2}+B+3I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0+2+3 & 0+1+0 \\ 0+(-4)+0 & 0+(-2)+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Consider the matrix B=[21−4−2]. Find f(B) if f(X)=X2+X+3.

a
[11−4−1]
b
[51−41]
c
[1141]
d
[41−51]
e
[5145]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

f(X)=X2+X+3=X2+X+3I

So, we want to find f(B)=B2+B+3I.

Let's calculate B2 as follows: B2=B⋅B=[21−4−2]⋅[21−4−2]=[0000]

Now, we can evaluate f(B):

f(B)=B2+B+3I=[0000]+[21−4−2]+3[1001]=[0000]+[21−4−2]+[3003]=[0+2+30+1+00+(−4)+00+(−2)+3]=[51−41]
